q: Magnetism is a phenomenon associated with _____.
e: Magnetism is a phenomenon associated with magnetic field. Magnetic field here means the region around a magnet where magnetic effects show up. Electric field: the influence around electric charge, not the field of a magnet.

q: A magnet has a _____ around it.
e: A magnet has a magnetic field around it. Magnetic field here means the region around a magnet where magnetic effects show up. Electric current: the flow of electric charge.

q: Magnets are materials which exhibit magnetic properties such as attracting magnetic materials, having two poles, and _____.
a: like poles attract, unlike poles repel
like poles repel, unlike poles attract
e: Magnets are materials which exhibit magnetic properties such as attracting magnetic materials, having two poles, and like poles repel, unlike poles attract. Like poles repel, unlike poles attract here means the two ends of a magnet, north and south. Like poles attract, unlike poles repel: the two ends of a magnet, north and south.

q: Magnetite consists of an oxide of _____.
e: Magnetite consists of an oxide of iron. Iron here means the metal in magnetite and the common magnetic element.

q: Materials such as cobalt, nickel, and some alloys such as steel are called _____.
e: Materials such as cobalt, nickel, and some alloys such as steel are called magnetic materials. Magnetic materials here means materials a magnet can attract, such as iron, cobalt, nickel, and steel. Non-magnetic materials: materials a magnet does not attract, such as brass, copper, wood, and plastic.

q: Materials such as brass, copper, wood, and plastics that are not attracted by a magnet are called _____.
e: Materials such as brass, copper, wood, and plastics that are not attracted by a magnet are called non-magnetic materials. Non-magnetic materials here means materials a magnet does not attract, such as brass, copper, wood, and plastic.

q: Any material that is able to keep its magnetism for a long time is called a _____.
e: Any material that is able to keep its magnetism for a long time is called a permanent magnet. Permanent magnet here means a body that attracts iron and has two poles. Temporary magnet: a body that attracts iron and has two poles.

q: Modern-day permanent magnets are usually made of steel and special alloys such as alcomax and _____.
e: Modern-day permanent magnets are usually made of steel and special alloys such as alcomax and alnico. Alnico here means an alloy used for strong permanent magnets, with aluminium, nickel, and cobalt.

q: Alcomax and alnico contain metals such as iron, nickel, copper, cobalt, and _____.
e: Alcomax and alnico contain metals such as iron, nickel, copper, cobalt, and aluminium. The physics in this sentence is built around aluminium.

q: Ceramic magnet is made from powders called _____.
e: Ceramic magnet is made from powders called ferrites. Every magnet has a north pole and a south pole, and like poles push apart.

q: Ferrites are compounds of iron oxide with _____.
e: Ferrites are compounds of iron oxide with other metal oxides. The physics in this sentence is built around other metal oxides.

q: Ceramic magnets are known to be _____.
e: Ceramic magnets are known to be brittle. Brittle here means easy to snap, the opposite of flexible.

q: The two ends of the magnet where most steel pins are attracted are called the _____ of the magnet.
e: The two ends of the magnet where most steel pins are attracted are called the poles of the magnet. Poles here means the two ends of a magnet, north and south.

q: When a suspended bar magnet comes to rest, one end always points towards the northern end of the Earth. This end is called the _____.
e: When a suspended bar magnet comes to rest, one end always points towards the northern end of the Earth. This end is called the north-seeking pole. Every magnet has a north pole and a south pole, and like poles push apart.

q: The north-seeking pole and south-seeking pole of the magnet are usually referred to as simply the north pole ($N$-pole) and the _____.
e: The north-seeking pole and south-seeking pole of the magnet are usually referred to as simply the north pole ($N$-pole) and the south pole ($S$-pole). Every magnet has a north pole and a south pole, and like poles push apart.

q: According to the law of magnetic poles, like poles _____ and unlike poles attract.
e: According to the law of magnetic poles, like poles repel and unlike poles attract. The physics in this sentence is built around repel.

q: A magnet can be used as a _____ for navigation.
e: A magnet can be used as a compass for navigation. Every magnet has a north pole and a south pole, and like poles push apart involving navigation.

q: Magnetic pole strength is a measure of the _____ of magnetic poles.
e: Magnetic pole strength is a measure of the strength of magnetic poles. The physics in this sentence is built around strength.

q: The force between two poles is directly proportional to the product of the pole strengths and _____ proportional to the distance squared between them.
e: The force between two poles is directly proportional to the product of the pole strengths and inversely proportional to the distance squared between them. The physics in this sentence is built around inversely.
